final_coverage_assessment: Coverage is good for the task window. National-level U.S. influenza surveillance data for MMWR Week 40 (Sep 29–Oct 5, 2024) is anchored by the CDC FluView report, which provides virological breakdown (56 influenza A viruses; 55.8% H1N1pdm09, 44.2% H3N2), percent positivity stability, ED visit trends, and a note on two H5 human cases in California. Subnational coverage is partially addressed by the Mississippi MSDH Week 40 PDF (ILI rate 2.8%, up from 2.3% prior week). PAHO Week 40 bulletin provides regional context for North America. ECDC CDTR covers the exact date range. News/specialist outlets (cidrap, contagionlive, reuters, etc.) are present in the accepted candidate pool and may yield additional evidence quotes. Gaps remain for: (a) explicit hospitalization counts (FluSurv-NET quantitative rates not confirmed in snippets); (b) confirmed deaths for the specific week; (c) subnational data beyond Mississippi. These gaps are consistent with the nature of early-season Week 40 data, where activity is at low/baseline levels and detailed hospitalization/mortality tables may not yet be populated.
final_trustworthiness_assessment: High. The primary source (CDC FluView 2024-week-40.html) is from the gold-standard U.S. influenza surveillance system on the cdc.gov domain. The MSDH PDF is from an official state health department (msdh.ms.gov) with explicit Week 40 dating. PAHO (paho.org) is an authoritative WHO regional office. ECDC (ecdc.europa.eu) is an authoritative EU public health agency. News/specialist sources (cidrap.umn.edu, reuters.com, contagionlive.com) are credible secondary sources. Low-trust results (facebook.com, wikipedia, statista) are present in the accepted pool but should be deprioritized or excluded during evidence extraction. The JMIR and PMC articles are peer-reviewed but cover prior seasons, not the specific task window.
